payload.report: A 70-year-old woman presents with a 6-month progressive pink, raised, non-tender 3 cm left breast lesion. Biopsy shows dermal confluent large lymphoid cells with epidermal ulceration, and immunohistochemistry is CD3/CD4/CD5/BCL2/MUM1/CD30 positive with Ki-67 95%, while cytokeratin/ALK1/MPO are negative. These findings refute malignant breast neoplasm and benign skin/breast lesions, and establish a primary cutaneous CD30+ T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder/lymphoma. Expert analyses (pathologist and radiologist) favor pcALCL over LyP, based on the solitary, continuously progressive, ulcerated lesion with BCL2/MUM1 positivity and very high Ki-67; systemic lymphoma with secondary skin involvement remains unlikely given localized disease without lymphadenopathy and ALK1 negativity. TCR clonality and systemic staging (PET/CT, LDH, bone marrow, lymph node evaluation) are still pending, so pcALCL is the leading diagnosis with staging required to exclude systemic disease.

frontier.label: Patient has primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma (pcALCL)
frontier.why: As a level 2 refinement of the broad CD30+ T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder/lymphoma category, pcALCL is now additionally supported by the radiologist's explicit preference over LyP. The persistent solitary 3 cm lesion and large CD30+ dermal T cells with BCL2/MUM1, Ki-67 95%, and ulceration favor pcALCL, but pending TCR clonality and systemic staging limit confidence to 0.5.
